Tooltip_morphine:
Instantly restores health, kills all pain, clears the mind
Does not heal wounds; highly addictive
Tooltip_naloxone:
Opioid antagonist; eases addiction.
Leaves you hungry and parched
Tooltip_fentanyl:
Fully restores health, clears the mind
Instantly addictive
Tooltip_oxycontin:
Restores a little health, calms the mind
Somewhat addictive
Tooltip_sufentanil:
Patch on the right upper arm: for days it keeps easing pain and holding you steady
Addiction keeps deepening
Tooltip_methamphetamine:
Days wide awake and strong
The crash will come
Tooltip_tranexamicacid:
Clots most of the bleeding
The clot turns into wound severity; dizzy weakness, nausea, lingering headache
Tooltip_sulfadimidine:
Clears most of a wound infection
The infection turns into wound severity; head pain, lingering fever, kidney strain, nausea
Tooltip_dexmedetomidine:
Small-animal veterinary sedative
Effect is a coin flip; heavy drowsiness, severe head pain
Tooltip_dextromethorphan:
Suppresses sneezing and coughing
Drowsy and parched; sleepiness takes over
Tooltip_GrassBandage: A crude emergency bandage of grass; all but guarantees wound infection
Tooltip_BookSplint: A splint lashed from two books
Tooltip_TemporarySplint:
Improvised fracture fixation
Does not heal the fracture -- unless worn for a very long time
Tooltip_AutoInjectorWatch:
An auto-injector watch. Tells time, date and temperature like any digital watch. Load one ampoule (morphine, naloxone, fentanyl or dexmedetomidine) through the right-click menu: while WORN, it injects automatically the moment overall health drops below a quarter. Right-click the watch to load or remove the ampoule.
Crafted by an experienced electrician.
